title: Leading coefficient bound for prime-to-p special-coset polynomials
statement:
Let $k\subseteq K$ be complete fields [def-weil-field] with compatible nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute values, and suppose $k$ is algebraically closed. Write $F^\circ=\{x\in F:|x|\le1\}$ for the valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring], $\widetilde F=F^\circ/\{x:|x|<1\}$ and $\Gamma_F=|F^	imes|$ for $F=k,K$. Suppose $\widetilde K=\widetilde k$, $\Gamma_K=\Gamma_k$, $p=\operatorname{char}\widetilde k>0$, and $K=k(z)^\wedge$ for $z
otin k$, where $k(z)^\wedge$ is the closure of the subfield generated by $k,z$. Put $r=\inf_{c\in k}|z-c|$. For $a\in K$ and $s>0$ define $S_{a,s}(K)=\{c^p-ac+e:c,e\in K,\ |pc^p|<s,\ |e|<s\}$. Let $b=\sum_{i=0}^m b_i z^i$ with $b_i\in k$, $b_m
e0$, $m\ge1$ and $p
mid m$. Assume $0
otin b+S_{a,s}(K)$, $\inf_{v\in b+S_{a,s}(K)}|v|=s$, and either $a=0$ or $(a,s)=(1,1)$. In the latter case assume also $|p b_i z^i|<1$ for every $1\le i\le m$. Then $|b_m|r^m\le s$, and if $m>1$ then $|b_m|r^m<s$.

source.place: Lemma 6.2.9, printed pp. 45–47, specialized to algebraically closed k; notation in the paragraphs before Lemma 6.2.7, printed p. 44.

proof.text: The radius $r$ is positive: otherwise a sequence of constants converging to $z$ is Cauchy in complete $k$, and its limit in $k$ equals $z$. It is unattained: if $|z-c|=r$, choose $d\in k^\times$ with $|d|=r$ using $\Gamma_K=\Gamma_k$, then lift the residue of $(z-c)/d$ from $\widetilde k$ to get $e\in k$ with $|z-(c+de)|<r$. Also $|p|<1$. Translate $z$ by a constant $c$ sufficiently close to $z$ that $|p||z-c|<r$ and $|z-c|\le|z|$, and rename the coordinate $z$. This preserves $r,b_m,m$ and $k(z)$. For the new coefficients $d_j=\sum_{i\ge j}\binom ij b_i c^{i-j}$, $j\ge1$, we have $|p d_j(z-c)^j|\le\max_{i\ge j}|p b_i z^i|<1$ in the $a=1$ case, since $|c|\le|z|$ and integral binomial coefficients have norm at most one. Thus all hypotheses survive, and henceforth $|pz|<r<|z|$.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 6.2.9, opening coordinate shift; pp. 44--45 for unattained type-4 radius.

proof.text: Obtain the isometric $k$-homomorphism $j:K\to D_r(K)$ with $j(z)=z+W$ from the translation-embedding node; step 1 verifies its radius hypotheses. Write $P=j(b)=\sum_{i=0}^m A_iW^i$, where $A_i=\sum_{j=i}^m\binom ji b_jz^{j-i}$. For every admissible $c,e\in K$, $j(b+c^p-ac+e)=P+j(c)^p-a j(c)+j(e)$, with unchanged norm and unchanged strict admissibility inequalities ($a=0$ or $1$). Consequently the infimum in the disc is at most $s$. The critical-coset calculus gives $|pb|<s$; isometry gives $\|pP\|_r< s$. Its nondiscrete-value-group hypothesis holds because algebraic closedness supplies roots of every $T^n-d$, so $\Gamma_k$ is divisible and is nontrivial.

source.place: Lemma 6.2.9, formula (1), the |pP| estimate and the extended-coset infimum, p. 46.

proof.text: First suppose $a=0$. If $|A_1|r>s$, choose an admissible disc element $P+C^p+H$ of norm $<|A_1|r$, which exists because its infimum is at most $s$. Put $C=\sum c_iW^i$. The linear coefficient of $C^p$ is $pc_0^{p-1}c_1$, and $|pc_0^{p-1}c_1|r\le |p|\|C\|_r^p=\|pC^p\|_r<s$: for this equality $C$ is an image $j(c)$, so its norm power is $|c|^p$. Indeed we may choose $c,e$ in $K$ already, since their original coset infimum is $s$. Also $|H_1|r<s$. Thus the linear coefficient cannot cancel $A_1$, a contradiction. Hence $|A_1|r\le s$. The polynomial $A_1=\sum_{i=1}^m i b_i z^{i-1}$ has degree $m-1$ and leading coefficient $mb_m$ of norm $|b_m|$, since $p\nmid m$. Factor it over $k$; its $m-1$ linear factors each have norm $>r$ by step 1. Therefore $|A_1|\ge |b_m|r^{m-1}$, strictly if $m>1$. Multiplication by $r$ proves both conclusions in this case.

source.place: Lemma 6.2.9(i), p. 46; algebraically closed specialization of Lemma 6.2.7 via linear factors.

proof.text: Now $a=s=1$. If $T:=|b_m|r^{m-1}\le |z|^{-1}$, then $|b_m|r^m\le r/|z|<1$ and we are done. Assume $T>|z|^{-1}$. Choose an algebraic closure $E$ of $K$ and extend its absolute value by the spectral-norm theorem. In $E$ choose $v$ with $v^{p^N}=z$, where $p^N\le m<p^{N+1}$; put $z_n=v^{p^{N-n}}$. Choose $\theta_n^{p^n}=A_{p^n}$ for $0\le n\le N$. Extend coefficients $D_r(K)\to D_r(E)$; this inclusion preserves the defining supremum norm, so the infimum from step 2 remains at most one. The disc obstruction applies to $P$ and these roots and gives $|\beta|r\le1$, where $\beta=\sum_{n=0}^N\theta_n$.

source.place: Lemma 6.2.9(ii), p. 46, reduced linear coefficient; p. 47, easy case |b_m|r^(m-1) <= |z|^(-1).

proof.text: For each $n\ge1$ put $q=p^n$. For every $j\ge q$ choose $h_{nj}\in k$ with $h_{nj}^q=\binom jq b_j$, and set $U_n=\sum_{j=q}^m h_{nj}z_n^{j-q}$. The root-sum estimate, applied to the summands of $A_q$, gives $|\theta_n-U_n|\le |p|^{1/q}\max_{j\ge q}|\binom jq b_j z^{j-q}|^{1/q}<|z|^{-1}<T$ in mixed characteristic: here each $|p b_j z^j|<1$. In equal characteristic the same estimate gives $\theta_n=U_n$. Put $U_0=A_1$ and $Q(v)=\sum_{n=0}^N U_n$. Then $|\beta-Q(v)|<T$ by the ultrametric inequality (if $N=0$ this difference is zero). Its coefficients belong to $k$ because $k$ is algebraically closed. Its degree in $v$ is $(m-1)p^N$, its leading coefficient is $mb_m$, and all terms from $n\ge1$ have smaller degree: $(m-p^n)p^{N-n}<(m-1)p^N$. Thus this polynomial is nonzero.

source.place: Lemma 6.2.9, formula (2) and the polynomial approximation beta-prime, p. 47; coefficients already have roots in k in this specialization.

proof.text: Put $q=p^N$ and $R=r^{1/q}$. We claim $\inf_{c\in k}|v-c|=R$, unattained. If $|c|^q>|z|$, ultrametricity gives $|v-c|^q=|c|^q=|z-c^q|$. Otherwise the prime-power difference estimate gives $|(v-c)^q-(z-c^q)|\le |p||z|<r<|z-c^q|$, hence again $|v-c|^q=|z-c^q|$. Every $d\in k$ equals $c^q$ for some $c\in k$, so taking infima gives $R$ and unattainment follows from step 1. Factor $Q$ over $k$. If $m>1$, each of its $(m-1)q$ factors has norm $>R$, so $|Q(v)|>|b_m|R^{(m-1)q}=T$. If $m=1$, it is the constant $b_m$ and has norm $T$. Since $|\beta-Q(v)|<T$, ultrametricity gives $|\beta|=|Q(v)|\ge T$, strictly if $m>1$. Combined with $|\beta|r\le1$ this proves the required weak and strict leading bounds.

source.place: Lemma 6.2.9, claim (*) and final application of Lemma 6.2.7, pp. 45 and 47; factorization proof in the algebraically closed case.

Step 1: r>0, unattained radius, shift with |pz|<r<|z|; the |p d_j z^j|<1 bound survives the shift because |c|<=|z|. Step 2: the translation-embedding and critical-coset statements apply; the value group is nondiscrete because it is divisible and nontrivial, giving ||pP||<s. Step 3 (a=0): the W-coefficient p c0^{p-1} c1 is bounded through isometry, and the linear-factorization leaf gives |A_1|>=|b_m|r^{m-1}, strict for m>1. Step 4: the spectral norm on the algebraic closure of complete K; the coefficient extension keeps inf<=1; the disc node gives r|beta|<=1. Step 5: root estimate (iii) gives error <|z|^-1<T, and the degree comparison (m-p^n)p^{N-n}<(m-1)p^N holds. Step 6: claim (*) is re-derived from difference estimate (ii), and factorization gives |beta|=|Q(v)|>=T. New root-estimate node: (i) multinomial divisibility; (ii) includes the p=2 sign term; (iii) holds for every root choice, via |zeta-1|<=|p|^{1/p^n} and a factor-norm argument. New disc node: true as stated; the mixed-characteristic nested-root errors are each <1/r because ||pP||<1, and missing roots can be taken in an extension, so it holds for arbitrary roots in E. Edge cases m=1, N=0, p=2 and equal characteristic were checked. No duplicates in the DAG and no restated clause.
